newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares recover some losses.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares recover some losses.

text.p: Norwegian shares made a slight recovery on Wednesday following two sessions of losses ahead of the annual results reporting period.
The Total share index advanced 0.4 percent to close at 1,075.49 points in healthy turnover of 1.1 billion crowns.
The banking, industry and shipping sectors all ended ahead, while the insurance index retreated.

"Bank shares are performing pretty much in line with the market, which is strong. The shares of the three top commercial banks are up 45 percent over a 12 month period, but so is the whole Norwegian market," said one analyst.

The banking index finished 3.18 ahead at 107.59 points after Norway's largest commercial bank, Den norske Bank, announced 1996 earnings up at 2.70 billion crowns from 2.66 billion in 1995. The bank said cost cuts and a healthy national economy helped lift 1996 net profits by 1.7 percent.
DnB closed 1.20 crowns higher at 28.90 crowns in turnover of 55.5 million crowns.

Seismic group Petroleum Geo-Services and power producer Hafslund both posted profits about in line with expectations and ended four crowns up at 269 crowns and 1.50 crowns higher at 50 crowns respectively. --Oslo newsroom +47 22 42 50 41
